Conversation so far:
Participant A (King Pasenadi): So, great king, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?

Write Participant B's next reply.

Sir, here in Sāvatthī a financier householder has passed away. Since he died childless, I have come after transferring his fortune to the royal compound. There was eight million in gold coin, not to mention the silver coin. And yet that financier ate meals of rough gruel with false black pepper. He wore clothes consisting of three patches of sunn hemp. He traveled around in a vehicle that was a dilapidated little cart, holding a leaf as parasol.
You are a Buddhist philosophical interlocutor. Reply naturally, reason from the source tradition, and keep the exchange grounded rather than generic.

Conversation so far:
Participant B (The Buddha): You speak well of them, who have let go the snares of Māra. Whose teaching did they understand to cut the bonds of rebirth?
Participant A (Ghaṭīkāra): None other than the Blessed One! None other than your instruction! It was your teaching that they understood to cut the bonds of rebirth. Where name and form cease with no residue left behind; understanding this teaching, they cut the bonds of rebirth.
Participant B (The Buddha): The words you say are deep, hard to understand, so very hard to wake up to. Whose teaching did you understand to be able to say such things?
Participant A (Ghaṭīkāra): In the past I was a potter in Vebhaliṅga called Ghaṭīkāra. I took care of my parents as a lay follower of Buddha Kassapa. I refrained from sexual intercourse, I was chaste, spiritual. We lived in the same village; in the past I was your comrade. I am the one who understands that these seven mendicants have been freed. With the complete ending of greed and hate, they've crossed over clinging to the world.

Write Participant B's next reply.

That's exactly how it was, just as you say, Bhaggava. In the past you were a potter in Vebhaliṅga called Ghaṭīkāra. You took care of your parents as a lay follower of Buddha Kassapa. You refrained from sexual intercourse, you were chaste, spiritual. We lived in the same village; in the past you were my comrade.

Conversation so far:
Participant A (King Pasenadi of Kosala): Does the worthy Gotama claim to have awakened to the supreme perfect awakening?

Write Participant B's next reply.
If anyone should rightly be said to have awakened to the supreme perfect awakening, it's me. For, great king, I have awakened to the supreme perfect awakening.

Participant B (a deity): Good fellow, do you know the liberation, emancipation, and seclusion of sentient beings?
Participant A (The Buddha): I do, good sir.

Write Participant B's next reply.
But how is it that you know the liberation, emancipation, and seclusion of sentient beings?

Conversation so far:
Participant B (Māra the Wicked): There's no escape in the world, so what will seclusion do for you? Enjoy erotic delights; don't regret it later.
Participant A (The Buddha): Who's speaking this verse, a human or a non-human?

Write Participant B's next reply.
This is Māra the Wicked, wanting to make me feel fear, terror, and goosebumps, wanting to make me fall away from seclusion!

Conversation so far:
Participant A (Rohitassa): Sir, is it possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there's no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn?

Write Participant B's next reply.
Reverend, I say it's not possible to know or see or reach the end of the world by traveling to a place where there's no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.

Conversation so far:
Participant A (Sakka): Rise, hero! Victor in battle, with burden put down, wander the world free of debt. Your mind is fully liberated, like the moon on the fifteenth night.

Write Participant B's next reply.

Lord of gods, that's not how to pay homage to the Realized Ones. This is how it should be done: 'Rise, hero! Victor in battle, caravan leader, wander the world free of debt. Let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma! There will be those who understand!'

Participant B (The Buddha): I gave the Buddha your message, and he accepted.
Participant A (Lohicca): Here, dear Rosika, go to the ascetic Gotama and announce the time, saying: 'It's time, worthy Gotama, the meal is ready.'
Participant B (The Buddha): Yes, worthy sir,
Participant A (Lohicca): Sir, please dissuade him from that harmful misconception.

Write Participant B's next reply.
Hopefully that'll happen, Rosika, hopefully that'll happen.

Participant A (Māra the Wicked): There's a mental snare wandering in midair. I'll bind you with ityou won't escape me, ascetic!

Sights, sounds, tastes, smells, and touches so delightful: desire for these is gone from me. You're beaten, terminator!
